prompt: Which display is best for showing the **shape** of a distribution with many values?
hint: Picture hundreds of values. A display that draws every single value would become crowded and hard to read.

hints.text: Picture hundreds of values. A display that draws every single value would become crowded and hard to read.
A dot plot needs one dot per value, and a box plot shows only five summary numbers. Think about the display that groups values into bins and draws a bar for each bin.
The best choice is the histogram (choice B), because its bars outline the shape of a large data set.

explanation: A dot plot draws one dot for every value, so with many values it becomes cluttered.
A box plot shows only the five-number summary, so peaks and clusters inside the data are hidden.
A histogram groups the values into bins, and the bar heights show where data piles up and where it thins out.
So the histogram, choice B, is best for showing the shape of a large distribution.
